questions.q: Which bond alternates headers and stretchers within each individual course?

questions.q: What geometric feature distinguishes a voussoir from an ordinary rectangular masonry unit?
o: It is always square in plan
Its side faces converge toward an arch center
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source describes the sides of a voussoir as converging toward one of the arch centers.

questions.q: In which bond are header and stretcher units intermingled in the same horizontal course?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: That mixed-header-and-stretcher arrangement is the defining feature of Flemish bond.

questions.q: For 12 mm plaster in the source table, what sand factor is used?

questions.n: Table 1.0 gives 0.012 m³ of sand per square metre for 12 mm plaster.

questions.q: What manufacturing process extrudes plastic clay through a die and cuts the continuous section to length with wires before firing?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source identifies this extrusion-and-wire-cut method as the stiff-mud process.

questions.q: What is the net exterior wall area to receive plaster after deducting all door and window openings?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 20–23 and Table 1.0 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: Gross wall area is 96.25 m². The total area of doors is 15.75 m² and windows total 11.30 m², leaving 69.20 m².

questions.q: If all openings are set back 0.10 m from the exterior face, how much additional plaster area is created by the reveals/returns?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 20–23 and Table 1.0 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The reveal area is based on the exposed perimeter of each opening multiplied by the 0.10 m recess depth, with door bottoms excluded.

questions.q: A brick is set on its long edge so that its short end appears at the wall face. What is this orientation called?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source identifies this long-edge placement with the end exposed as a rowlock.

questions.q: How much sand is required for the same 12 mm plaster work?

questions.n: The table gives 0.012 m³ of sand per square metre for 12 mm plaster. Multiplying by 69.20 m² gives 0.8304 m³.

questions.q: A restoration detail requires replacement of one tapered masonry block from an arch ring. What is the correct technical term for that block?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: An individual wedge-shaped unit forming an arch is a voussoir.

questions.q: Which masonry wall type is tied back to a separate structural frame, such as wood or metal studs?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source identifies masonry veneer as the masonry skin attached to a separate structural frame.

questions.q: A 40 m² wall is to receive 12 mm plaster. Using 0.012 m³ of sand per square metre, what sand volume is required?

questions.q: A wall pattern alternates a header, then a stretcher, repeatedly within the same course. Which bond should be specified?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: Flemish bond alternates header and stretcher units within each course.

questions.q: Which bond alternates whole header courses with whole stretcher courses?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source defines English bond by alternating all-header and all-stretcher courses.

questions.q: What is the source's term for the movement joint between a building frame and its cladding skin?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 26–27, 93–95, 151, 153–155 (substantially reworded)
questions.n: The source classifies the independent frame-to-cladding attachment as a structure/enclosure joint.
